text: Latent class models assume items independent within class. bvr() gives bivariate residual every pair categorical indicators (Pearson chi-square observed model-implied two-way table, divided df; Mplus TECH10): pair large BVR can modelled jointly within-class log-linear association (Hagenaars 1988), class-specific (association = "varying", pair one joint item) equal across classes: continuous indicators, lpa(..., = list(c(y1, y2))) frees selected within-class covariances (Mplus y1 y2).

title: Getting started with latentmixtures
text: aces holds retrospective reports eight adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) 1,500 adults: emotional, physical sexual abuse, emotional physical neglect, witnessed domestic violence, household substance misuse household mental illness, coded 0/1 2% missing. data generated four classes (Low adversity, Household dysfunction, Maltreatment, High adversity; shares 0.52, 0.20, 0.17, 0.11). Choose indicators tidyselect number classes K. starts mirrors Mplus STARTS; default 100 random starts 20 EM iterations, best 20 iterated convergence. printout shows fit statistics (log-likelihood, number free parameters, AIC, BIC, sample-size adjusted BIC, entropy, smallest class often best log-likelihood replicated), class sizes average posterior probabilities, item-response probabilities. four generating classes recovered: large low-adversity class, maltreatment class (abuse neglect), household-dysfunction class (violence, substance misuse, mental illness) small class high probabilities everything. Missing responses handled full-information maximum likelihood; rows every item missing analysed. classify() returns one row per input row (NA rows analysed), can bound data: Indicators may numeric codes, factors, characters logicals; factor labels used output. code: library(latentmixtures) lm_available()               # TRUE once Julia and LatentMixtures.jl are installed lm_start(threads = 4)        # optional: starts Julia once; fitting functions auto-start it  # LCA: eight adverse childhood experiences (ace_*) of 1,500 adults. Which patterns of # childhood adversity are there? (generated with four classes) data(aces) m4 <- aces |> lca(starts_with("ace_"), K = 4) convergence(m4)              # check that the best LL is replicated and EM reached the maximum m4                           # header, fit, class sizes, item-response probabilities summary(m4)                  # every parameter with robust standard errors head(classify(m4))           # posterior probabilities and modal class per row  # covariates, known groups, weights: also columns of the data lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4, covariates = c(female, low_parent_edu), weights = weight) lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4, group = female, invariance = "ace_sex_abuse")  # LPA: sleep, activity, diet, stress, loneliness and life satisfaction data(wellbeing) lpa(wellbeing, sleep:lifesat, K = 4, variances = "varying") # mixed indicator types: binary ACE items with an overdispersed symptom count (Mplus COUNT) mixture(aces, K = 4, categorical = starts_with("ace_"), negbin = depress) # LTA: alcohol, binge drinking, cigarettes and cannabis in grades 8, 10 and 12 data(substance) t3 <- lta(substance, waves = list(alc_1:mj_1, alc_2:mj_2, alc_3:mj_3), K = 3) transitions(t3) # growth mixtures: depressive (dep1-dep5) and anxiety (anx1-anx5) symptoms, ages 12-16 data(depression) g <- growth(depression, dep1:dep5, K = 4, model = "gmm", degree = 2) growth(depression, processes = list(dep1:dep5, anx1:anx5), K = 4, model = "gmm") # two-level LCA: students in schools, 3 student classes and 2 latent school types data(schools) ml <- lca(schools, starts_with("b_"), K = 3, level2 = school, KB = 2) conditionalprobs(ml)         # P(student class | school type)  # three-step auxiliary models: model, data, columns r3step(m4, aces, c(female, age, low_parent_edu), ref = 1)   # who is in which class?
